decided.question: does the seed grow to cover `saas` and an `access` topic for `other`, or does the coverage claim go
decided.chose: the coverage claim is deleted from Seed Data and the two uncovered kinds are recorded as a Known Gap
decided.rejected: adding a SaaS access topic and an access-type Other row to the seed table
decided.why: rule 1 — an `access` topic named `Other` cannot exist beside the seeded question `Other`, because REQ-02-006 makes a name unique per organization and audience, so the claim could not be made true as the table stands; and what a starting catalogue should contain is a product choice, not a repair
decided.recordedAt: the fourth row of Known Gaps in 02-request-topics.md, which names `saas` and the `access` `other`, says the seed is a starting catalogue rather than a migration of the retired vocabulary, notes the REQ-02-006 collision that rejects the alternative, and gives a later revision of the seed table as what closes it

decided.question: does the catalogue ship a drag handle or up and down controls
decided.chose: up and down controls; the Settings mock draws [▲] and [▼] on each active row and no drag handle
decided.rejected: the drag handle the mock drew
decided.why: rule 1 — the `@ds` barrel exports no drag or sortable primitive, so the mock asked for a component the design system cannot supply; and rule 3 — a pointer-only handle is unreachable from the keyboard
decided.recordedAt: the paragraph under the Settings mock in the contracts, which states the controls, the single PATCH each issues, that the first row draws no up control and the last no down one, and that the archived list draws neither; the DS gaps row now reads 'as the mock draws them', and the two ids are in the Required data-testid table and TC-02-E2E-01

decided.question: does PATCH …/request-topics/{topicId} refuse a supplied `type` or ignore it
decided.chose: a different `type` is refused with 400 REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.typeImmutable; a `type` equal to the stored value is accepted and changes nothing, exactly as the sibling `audience` behaves
decided.why: rule 2 — the same route already refuses a changed `audience` with audienceImmutable, and REQ-02-022 refuses rather than drops a classifier the server owns; the wording 'not accepted' is gone from the contract
decided.recordedAt: REQ-02-004, retitled 'the audience and the kind are immutable', with the rejected reading in its second Decided paragraph; the message row, the PATCH route's Errors cell, validation rule 3a and TC-02-INT-06 all carry typeImmutable

decided.question: is the `topic` response member keyed on `topicId` or on `topicLabel`
decided.chose: keyed on `topicLabel` — `topic` is null exactly when the request carries no label, and `topic.id`, `audience`, `type` and `status` are each null when a labelled request carries no `topicId`
decided.rejected: keying on `topicId`, which would serve `topic: null` for a request that does carry a snapshot name
decided.why: rule 3 — the label is what the request is about and is written once, so the reading that keeps showing it loses nothing, and it gives one shape to the state TC-02-INT-02 creates
decided.recordedAt: the paragraph under the `topic` member of the POST …/requests contract, and the Expected Result of TC-02-INT-02, which asserts that shape; the Data Model row for `topicId` now says SetNull fires through no route this spec exposes rather than claiming it never fires in practice

decided.question: which audience gates the new-request form when it has no active topic
decided.chose: the addressee's audience, which is `staff` while `member` is the only addressee kind a request may carry (REQ-02-020); an empty `client` audience leaves the form usable
decided.rejected: any audience, which would withdraw a working staff picker over the half of the catalogue the form cannot reach
decided.why: rule 2 — AC-16, edge case 13 and TC-02-E2E-06 all read `staff`, so the surrounding text already takes this reading and only the requirement did not say it
decided.recordedAt: REQ-02-017, whose rule names the audience of the form's addressee and whose second Decided paragraph states the rejected reading
